symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the propensity score.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the control regression.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the conditional effect.

symbols.name: sim_1
symbols.def: \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\) when the samples differ by replacement of at most one record.

symbols.name: R_NP
symbols.def: Nonprivate minimax absolute risk on \(\mathcal M_H\).

symbols.name: R_DP
symbols.def: Pure-private minimax absolute risk on \(\mathcal M_H\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: Auxiliary coin, independent record by record.

symbols.name: a_bar
symbols.def: Fixed public amplitude chosen so that \(t b_h\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L/4)\) whenever \(|t|\le\bar a h^\gamma\).

symbols.name: Lambda
symbols.def: Public indices of bounded compactly supported wavelets on \([0,1]^d\).

symbols.name: Xi
symbols.def: Public nuisance-sign codebook containing precisely the retained legal wavelet profiles.

symbols.name: v_xi
symbols.def: \(v_\xi(x)=\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}\xi_\ell c_\ell\psi_\ell(x)\), with the public coefficients chosen so every retained profile lies in \(\mathcal H^\beta(L/4)\).

symbols.name: M_grid
symbols.def: Positive target-grid half-width in index units.

symbols.name: P_j_xi
symbols.def: Law indexed by \((j,\xi)\) with uniform \(X\), randomized treatment, binary potential outcomes, \(\mu_0=v_\xi\), and \(\mu_1=v_\xi+t_jb_h\).

symbols.name: H_coupled
symbols.def: Form bounded pair contrasts within public wavelet cells, cap cell occupancies before Hamming stabilization, profile the resulting composite scores inside each target slab, and apply scalar-shell selection only after the nuisance profiles have been absorbed.

standard.name: Fixed interior evaluation point in Theorem 1

novel.justification: This regime isolates observational designs with a smoother effect surface than the combined treatment and baseline nuisances; it is retained unchanged from the destination model.
Exact uniform random design is the unchanged destination model and is realized by benchmark studies that sample covariate locations from a public uniform design.

standard.name: Uniform overlap in Section 1 and Proposition S5

novel.justification: This range includes fixed and polynomially vanishing central-privacy budgets down to the saturation boundary and is retained unchanged from the destination problem.
Binary treatment responses occur directly and are also obtained exactly from any bounded response by recordwise randomized preprocessing that preserves conditional means.

definitions.name: Exact-uniform coupled-nuisance Hölder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_H=\{P:(P,Y_0,Y_1,A,X)\text{ induces }O\in\mathcal O\text{ and satisfies }\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:exchangeability},\text{ass:uniform-design},\text{ass:overlap},\text{ass:propensity-holder},\text{ass:control-holder},\text{ass:effect-holder},\text{ass:low-nuisance}\}\), indexed by \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,q,L,e_0,x_0\).

definitions.name: Recordwise Bernoullization kernel
definitions.construction: For each record draw an independent \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), set \(B=2\mathbf 1\{U\le(Y+1)/2\}-1\), and output \(K_B(O)=(B,A,X)\).

definitions.name: Finite baseline-regression profiles
definitions.construction: Choose public \(\Lambda\), coefficients \(c_\ell\), and codebook \(\Xi\), and construct \(v_\xi(x)=\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}\xi_\ell c_\ell\psi_\ell(x)\) for every \(\xi\in\Xi\), retaining only profiles with \(\|v_\xi\|_\infty\le1/4\) and \(v_\xi\in\mathcal H^\beta(L/4)\).

definitions.name: Localized target profiles and scalar grid
definitions.construction: Set \(C_h=x_0+[-h/2,h/2]^d\), \(b_h(x)=\kappa((x-x_0)/h)\), \(p_h=h^d\), \(c_h=p_h^{-1}\int_{C_h}b_h\), \(a_h=\bar a h^\gamma\), \(r=a_h/M_{\mathrm{grid}}\), and \(t_j=jr\) for \(-M_{\mathrm{grid}}\le j\le M_{\mathrm{grid}}\).

definitions.name: Explicit finite target-fiber experiment
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{-M_{\mathrm{grid}},\ldots,M_{\mathrm{grid}}\}\) and \(\xi\in\Xi\), construct \(P_{j,\xi}\) by drawing \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), drawing \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \((Y_0,Y_1)\) given \(X\), drawing \(Y_0,Y_1\in\{-1,1\}\) conditionally independently with means \(v_\xi(X)\) and \(v_\xi(X)+t_jb_h(X)\), and setting \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\); set \(F_j=\{P_{j,\xi}:\xi\in\Xi\}\).

definitions.name: Scalar-shell exponential selector
definitions.construction: Draw \(J_\epsilon\) with \(P(J_\epsilon=j\mid D_n)=e^{-\epsilon Q_j(D_n)/2}/\sum_{l=-M_{\mathrm{grid}}}^{M_{\mathrm{grid}}}e^{-\epsilon Q_l(D_n)/2}\), and return \(T_{\mathrm{shell}}(D_n)=t_{J_\epsilon}\).

definitions.name: Unknown-propensity extension handle
definitions.construction: Use \(H_{\mathrm{coupled}}\): build bounded pair contrasts within public wavelet cells, cap cell occupancies before taking a Hamming envelope, profile the composite score over the nuisance profiles in each target slab, and feed only the profiled target scores to the scalar-shell selector.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_H\), the recordwise image \(K_BP\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\pm}\) and has the same \(P_X\), \(\pi\), \(\mu_0\), \(\mu_1\), and \(\tau(x_0)\). Coupling the auxiliary coins on unchanged records maps \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\) to Bernoullized samples differing in at most one record.
statements.justification: The reduction removes arbitrary conditional outcome distributions without changing the causal target or privacy adjacency.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. allow bounded outcomes and use binary submodels for converses, but do not state this two-sided privacy-preserving experiment map.
statements.consumer: Finite-alphabet target-fiber mechanisms can be transferred to bounded-outcome CATE without a risk penalty.

statements.justification: Conditional Jensen gives the nonprivate direction, while coupled recordwise preprocessing gives the private direction on every input dataset.
statements.gap: Private coupling inequalities do not by themselves give equality of both constrained and unconstrained CATE minimax risks under Bernoullization.
statements.consumer: Binary-outcome upper constructions and lower bounds apply exactly to the original bounded-response model.

statements.statement: For every retained \(\xi\in\Xi\) and every \(-M_{\mathrm{grid}}\le j\le M_{\mathrm{grid}}\), \(P_{j,\xi}\in\mathcal M_{\pm}\subset\mathcal M_H\), \(\pi_{P_{j,\xi}}\equiv1/2\), \(\mu_{0,P_{j,\xi}}=v_\xi\), and \(\tau_{P_{j,\xi}}(x)=t_jb_h(x)\), so \(\tau_{P_{j,\xi}}(x_0)=t_j\).
statements.justification: This verifies that the explicit finite experiment is a genuine target-fiber subexperiment of the unchanged causal class rather than a stand-in regression model.
statements.gap: Generic finite hypothesis families need not preserve the causal factorization, Hölder radii, or the exact pointwise target.
statements.consumer: The shell certificate below becomes an internally valid CATE theorem with arbitrary finite nuisance multiplicity.

statements.statement: For a universal numerical constant \(c>0\) and every \(P=P_{j,\xi}\), \(\mathbb E_P Z_h=t_j\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_h)\le4/(np_hc_h^2)\), and \(Z_h\) has replacement sensitivity at most \(\Delta_h=4/(np_hc_h)\). Hence every \(Q_l\) has replacement sensitivity at most one and, for every \(u>0\), \(P(|Z_h-t_j|>u)\le2\exp\{-c\min(np_hc_h^2u^2,np_hc_hu)\}\), uniformly in \(j\), \(\xi\), and \(K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\).
statements.justification: Randomized treatment makes the localized pseudo-outcome exactly orthogonal to every baseline wavelet profile, leaving a bounded scalar statistic with explicit global sensitivity.
statements.gap: The parent construction controls separately released nuisance coordinates; it does not expose an all-dataset one-sensitive score whose law is uniform over an arbitrary nuisance codebook.
statements.consumer: The concentration and sensitivity inequalities provide every quantitative input for the distance-weighted shell theorem.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C_0,c_0,C_1>0\), depending only on \(\kappa\), such that if \(np_h\ge1\) and \(r\ge C_0\max\{(np_h)^{-1/2},(n\epsilon p_h)^{-1}\}\), then for every \(i\in\{-M_{\mathrm{grid}},\ldots,M_{\mathrm{grid}}\}\), every \(P\in F_i\), and every integer \(k\ge1\), \[\sum_{j:\,|j-i|=k}\mathbb E_P\!\left[1\wedge\exp\left\{-\frac{\epsilon}{2}(Q_j-Q_i)\right\}\right]\le6e^{-c_0k}.\] Consequently, \[\sum_{k\ge1}(k+1)\sum_{j:\,|j-i|=k}\mathbb E_P\!\left[1\wedge\exp\left\{-\frac{\epsilon}{2}(Q_j-Q_i)\right\}\right]\le6\frac{e^{-c_0}(2-e^{-c_0})}{(1-e^{-c_0})^2}.\] Every \(Q_j\) is one-sensitive, \(T_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private, and \(\sup_{P\in\bigcup_iF_i}\mathbb E_P|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-\tau_P(x_0)|\le C_1r\), where \(C_1\) is independent of \(M_{\mathrm{grid}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\). For this ordered finite family, this strictly tightens the direct cover-based application of Theorem 13 and Proposition 16 of Asi et al., whose guarantee counts all \((2M_{\mathrm{grid}}+1)K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\) candidate laws; it also removes the nuisance-cardinality term certified by the parent joint-release construction because no nuisance coordinate is released.
statements.justification: On the event \(|Z_h-t_i|\le kr/4\), the score gap is at least \(kr/(2\Delta_h)\); Bernstein controls the complement by \(2e^{-c k}\), and at most two target indices lie in each shell, giving the displayed geometric series without a union bound.
statements.gap: Asi et al. retain cover cardinality in their universal T-mechanism, while the parent joint release pays for nuisance profiles. The theorem gives an explicit checkable shell inequality whose constant is independent of both target-grid and nuisance-profile cardinalities.
statements.consumer: Finite privacy audits can enlarge the baseline wavelet codebook without changing the certified CATE risk, isolating coupled unknown propensity rather than nuisance enumeration as the remaining obstruction.

statements.statement: When \(d=1\), \(\gamma=1\), and \(\pi(x)=1/2\), a public bandwidth localized release based on \(W_{\mathrm{rt}}\) attains uniform absolute risk \(C\max\{n^{-1/3},(n\epsilon)^{-1/2}\}\) over the randomized-treatment subclass of \(\mathcal M_H\), and the matching direct-bump lower bound holds. Taking \(h\asymp r\) in Theorem 5 recovers the same rate on every explicit finite wavelet subexperiment without logarithms.
statements.justification: This reduction checks the bandwidth, sensitivity, and pointwise privacy balance against a standard nonparametric regression problem.
statements.gap: Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen analyze central-private pointwise nonparametric regression through wavelet release; the proposition supplies the exact causal pseudo-outcome reduction, bounded-response pure-private rate, and scalar-shell implementation.
statements.consumer: The result is a same-class benchmark for randomized trials and a falsification check for the finite-fiber theorem.

statements.statement: Can \(H_{\mathrm{coupled}}\) produce one-sensitive profiled scores on the full unknown-propensity class \(\mathcal M_H\) whose distance-weighted shell sum is bounded independently of the wavelet-sieve size whenever \(r\ge C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\), using the same sample size \(n\) and no released nuisance coordinates? The required certificate must control random cell occupancies and arbitrary dependence in least-favorable nuisance mixtures.
statements.justification: The finite theorem proves that nuisance cardinality is removable under exact randomized-treatment orthogonalization; unknown propensity introduces the genuinely second-order score-stability problem.
statements.gap: Neither Asi et al.'s cover theorem nor the parent's lower-envelope coupling supplies a stable composite upper score for arbitrary dependent nuisance priors.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would be the missing upper mechanism needed to turn the inherited lower envelope into the global symbolic pure-private pointwise-CATE frontier.

sampling_model.design: The ambient model has known \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) and independent observed records; the headline finite experiment further has \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent causal units with bounded observed outcomes in \([-1,1]\); the finite certificate uses the binary subexperiment obtained by exact Bernoullization.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with conditional exchangeability and uniform overlap in the ambient class, specialized to randomized treatment for the unconditional finite-fiber theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite baseline regression ranges over \(K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\) public wavelet profiles, but the mechanism neither estimates nor releases their indices.

bibliography.citation: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman. Minimax rates for heterogeneous causal effect estimation. \emph{Annals of Statistics}, 52(2):793--816, 2024. Theorems 1--2 and Section 5.

Hilal Asi, John C. Duchi, Saminul Haque, Zewei Li, and Feng Ruan. Universally instance-optimal mechanisms for private statistical estimation. \emph{Proceedings of Machine Learning Research}, 247:221--259, 2024. Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16.

T. Tony Cai, Abhinav Chakraborty, and Lasse Vuursteen. Optimal federated learning for nonparametric regression with heterogeneous distributed differential privacy constraints. Public preprint, arXiv:2406.06755, 2024. Sections 2 and 3.3, Theorem 3.4, and Theorem 4.4.

Clément L. Canonne, Gautam Kamath, Audra McMillan, Adam Smith, and Jonathan Ullman. The structure of optimal private tests for simple hypotheses. \emph{Proceedings of the ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing}, 2019. Theorem 1.2 and Section 2.
Jayadev Acharya, Ziteng Sun, and Huanyu Zhang. Differentially private Assouad, Fano, and Le Cam. \emph{Proceedings of Machine Learning Research}, 132:48--78, 2021. Theorems 1 and 3.

Fengshi Niu, Harsha Nori, Brian Quistorff, Rich Caruana, Donald Ngwe, and Aadharsh Kannan. Differentially private estimation of heterogeneous causal effects. \emph{Proceedings of the Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning}, 2022. Theorem 6.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 13 and Proposition 16 give a universal pure-private scalar T-mechanism guarantee with finite-cover logarithmic dependence.
Theorems 1--2 derive and attain the nonprivate pointwise-CATE minimax rate in a Hölder model.
Section 3.3 and Theorems 3.4 and 4.4 give upper and lower guarantees for pointwise nonparametric regression under distributed differential privacy, including the single-server central model.
Theorem 1.2 characterizes pure-private simple-hypothesis testing up to constants through clamped likelihood ratios.
Theorem 1 converts expected-Hamming couplings of hypothesis mixtures into central-private Le Cam lower bounds.
Theorem 6 proves privacy composition for a sample-split CATE meta-algorithm without a Hölder pointwise minimax utility theorem.

tldr: The theorem-level contribution is an unconditional, nuisance-cardinality-free shell certificate for an explicit finite pointwise-CATE subexperiment of the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder class. The family contains an arbitrary finite codebook of baseline wavelet profiles and localized target bumps under randomized treatment. A single bounded pseudo-outcome score is one-sensitive, its target-distance shells have a uniform geometric summability bound, and scalar exponential selection achieves risk \(O(r)\) without dependence on either the target-grid size or the nuisance codebook size. This strictly tightens the cover-based guarantee of Asi et al. on this ordered family and the parent joint-release certificate, while the unknown-propensity full-class frontier remains an open extension rather than a claimed theorem.

project_justification.gap: General private T-mechanisms count a finite cover, and the parent pointwise-CATE upper construction releases target and nuisance coordinates jointly. Neither gives a theorem-level distance-weighted shell inequality whose constant stays fixed as the nuisance codebook grows.
project_justification.niche: Randomized treatment exactly orthogonalizes the CATE pseudo-outcome against a high-cardinality baseline-regression fiber while preserving the causal target and all ambient Hölder assumptions.
project_justification.fill: The explicit finite wavelet family, localized score, replacement sensitivity, per-shell exponential bound, and closed geometric summability constant provide a complete finite-fiber mechanism theorem. The global symbolic frontier is not asserted because the certificate does not yet treat unknown propensity.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024), Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, define the ambient Hölder pointwise-CATE benchmark and its nonprivate higher-order geometry; their result is inherited background, not a theorem promise here. Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan (2024), Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16, provide the closest mechanism comparator: applying their cover-based T-mechanism directly to the present finite experiment counts all target and nuisance candidates, whereas Theorem 5 proves a geometric shell sum independent of \(K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\) and \(M_{\mathrm{grid}}\). The parent joint-release construction is a non-archival internal comparator whose certified error contains nuisance-net multiplicity; Theorem 5 removes that term on the explicit randomized-treatment family by never releasing a nuisance coordinate. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024), Section 3.3 and Theorems 3.4 and 4.4, analyze pointwise nonparametric regression under distributed privacy, with the single-server case providing the direct central-private regression comparator for Proposition 6; their wavelet coefficient release does not establish the causal target-fiber shell inequality. Canonne et al. (2019) inform the one-sensitive testing architecture, and Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021) inform the inherited full-class converse, but neither resolves composite unknown-propensity upper scores. Niu et al. (2022), Theorem 6, is a concrete private CATE consumer without a pure-private pointwise Hölder minimax theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The score \(Q_j\) eliminates baseline-wavelet multiplicity because \(\pi\equiv1/2\) makes \(W_{\mathrm{rt}}\) conditionally unbiased for \(\tau\). With unknown propensity, singleton mixtures from separated target fibers can coincide, so the same one-record score cannot certify the full class. The proposed pair-contrast handle must control random occupancies and dependent nuisance priors; no global upper frontier follows from the finite theorem.
honest_scope: The unconditional headline covers explicit finite target fibers with arbitrary finite baseline-wavelet codebooks inside the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder CATE class, under randomized treatment and pure central privacy. It proves the nuisance-cardinality-free distance-weighted shell inequality and its private risk consequence. The ambient Bernoulli equivalence and the randomized-treatment reduction are supporting results. The inherited exact-uniform lower envelope is background only. The full unknown-propensity symbolic frontier remains Open-ended Question 7, so no equality involving \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\), \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), \(r_G\), and \(r_F\) is claimed. When \(d=1\) and \(\gamma=1\), choosing \(h\asymp r\) reduces the finite certificate to the known pointwise regression balance \(\max\{n^{-1/3},(n\epsilon)^{-1/2}\}\).
literature_map: Kennedy et al. fix the ambient nonprivate CATE model. Asi et al. supply the cover-based private T-mechanism whose candidate-count step is strictly tightened on the explicit finite family. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen supply the direct central-private pointwise regression comparison for the randomized-treatment reduction. Canonne et al. and Acharya et al. delimit the simple-test and coupling tools relevant to the still-open unknown-propensity extension, while Niu et al. provide an applied private CATE consumer.
novelty_justification: The theorem does not claim the unresolved global frontier. Its strict advance is a fully specified finite causal experiment with arbitrarily many baseline wavelet profiles for which the score, replacement sensitivity, shell indexing, per-shell exponential inequality, and total distance-weighted sum are all explicit and independent of nuisance cardinality. This is stronger than applying the published cover-based T-mechanism or the parent joint-release certificate to the same family.
message: Revised the full proposal core around an unconditional finite-fiber shell theorem with explicit scores, sensitivity, geometric summability, and nuisance-cardinality-free risk; the unsupported global frontier is retained only as an open question.
